items.title: Terry Gibbs interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2001 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: And then when I got to work with him, it was amazing.

ctx.x: Is that where you got most of your exposure?

Well no, they had the big bands at the Paramount Theater and the Strand Theater. Never in my born days did I ever think I would ever work with Benny Goodman. When I was a kid I’d be the first one in line, five or six o’clock in the morning, to get in the Paramount Theater. And when that stage would go up in the old days, and people would go to the Paramount Theater, that stage used to rise. And while it was going up from the pit, Benny would be playing the theme song “Let’s Dance.” My hair would stand up. And…
He could. What’s that, there’s some story I heard about Gubenko, him calling someone Gubenko.

items.title: Terry Gibbs interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 5, 2021 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: When I was 25 years old and he was 42 I played with Benny.

ctx.x: You know I did want to be a boxer at one time but it was either that — but I realized playing music was more important to me. I don’t think there’s anything I actually wanted to do that, you know something Monk? I may have had a lot of mishaps but we all — I’m 97 years old now and we all have had some rainy days. You know. But I am blessed with being, in my 97 years maybe two years of it I would say were dumb, were just something — it’s not I regret, it’s something I couldn’t do anything about. There was a point…

blessed as I was. If you look at the pictures in the book, all those people, first of all Benny Goodman was the King of Swing. When I was 25 years old and he was 42 I played with Benny. After four bars we were the same age. Music has no numbers. Same age. I mean I wrote about this, not only did I play with Charlie Parker but he worked for me one time for four weeks. But Dizzy Gillespie, who was my friend, who heard me play because I worked opposite him a lot of time, I was sitting by a music store when I was…
Well you answered my next question. I was going to ask you —
